trial_court: IV Additional Principal Judge, Family Court, Bengaluru, M.C.No.2308/2013
facts_of_case: Petitioner filed petition under Section 13(1)(ia)&(ib) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, which was dismissed by the trial court. The parties have now reached a compromise and the marriage is dissolved by decree of divorce.

legal_principles.principle: A compromise arrived at between the parties can be a valid ground for dismissing a petition.
legal_principles.held: They have invited attention of this Court to the memo filed on behalf of the parties, which has been duly signed by them.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party seeking to set aside a compromise to prove that it was not voluntary.
legal_principles.held: They have invited attention of this Court to the memo filed on behalf of the parties, which has been duly signed by them.

outcome.result: Appeal disposed of in terms of the compromise arrived at between the parties
outcome.final_order: Marriage performed on 23.04.2007 is dissolved by a decree of divorce, and the appellant shall pay a sum of Rs.4,00,000/- to the respondent.

keywords: C/c. Of I Additional Principal Judge
Latin maxim: Nemo judex in causa sua
